html:
The Battle of Kleidion was fought on 29 July 1014 in a valley of the Belasitsa mountains, in what is now southwestern Bulgaria near the border with North Macedonia. Emperor Basil II crushed the army of Tsar Samuel of Bulgaria there, after nearly half a century of war.

The Bulgarians had walled off the pass. While Basil attacked the wall from the front, his general Nikephoros Xiphias led a force over the mountain and fell on the Bulgarians from behind, and their army broke.

According to the chronicler John Skylitzes, Basil blinded the 15,000 prisoners, leaving one man in every hundred with one eye to lead the rest home. When Samuel saw them he collapsed, and he died two days later. Modern historians think the number is probably too high, but the story gave Basil his name, the Bulgar-slayer.

Resistance lasted four more years, until the whole Bulgarian state was annexed in 1018. It stayed in the Byzantine Empire until the uprising of Asen and Peter in 1185.
